title: Mass and liquid volume

sections.label: A
sections.instruction: How much water is in each container? Write the amount.

design.purpose: Read a liquid volume in liters from a scale marked every liter.
design.rationale: 3.MD.A.2 asks students to measure liquid volume, not only to compute with it. The scale is a vertical number line with only every second mark numbered, so students count on from the nearest number.
misconceptions: Reading the nearest numbered mark instead of the mark the water reaches.
Treating each mark as 2 because the numbers go up by 2.

sections.label: B
sections.instruction: How much water is in each container? Write the amount.

design.purpose: Read a liquid volume in milliliters from a scale marked every 50 milliliters.
design.rationale: A jug marked in 50s makes students find the value of one mark before reading the level. It is the same skill as reading a scaled bar graph.
misconceptions: Counting each mark as 1 or 10 milliliters.

design.purpose: Solve one-step problems about mass in grams and kilograms, and liquid volume in liters.
design.rationale: Every problem stays in one unit, so the arithmetic is the only step. The problems use multiplication and subtraction, as 3.MD.A.2 allows, with numbers students can work mentally or on paper.
misconceptions: Thinking a heavier object must be bigger.
Adding the two masses when the question asks how much heavier.

design.purpose: Measure liquid volume from a scale, then solve one-step problems about mass and volume.
design.rationale: Students read liters from a scale marked every liter, then milliliters from a scale marked every 50. The word problems that follow use the same units, so measuring comes before computing.

advice: "How much water is in each container? Write the amount." is practice, and nothing on the sheet introduces it with a worked example.
